MGIMS Hosts National Conference on Collaborative Maternal Healthcare
Monday, 24 March 2025
1450 Hits
On March 22 and 23, 2025, the Mahatma Gandhi Institute of Medical Sciences (MGIMS), Sevagram, organized a two-day conference on "Current Concepts in the Collaborative Care Model for Improving Holistic Healthcare of Mothers and Their Babies" in association with the Safe Motherhood Committee, FOGSI, and the World Health Organization (WHO). Dr. Pawan Kumar, Additional Commissioner of Maternal Health & Immunization, MOHFW, New Delhi, graced the event as the esteemed Chief Guest, while Dr. Priyanka Singh from WHO was the Guest of Honor. The event was also attended by distinguished dignitaries, including Dr. B. S. Garg (Secretary, Kasturba Health Society), Dr. A. K. Shukla (Dean, MGIMS), Dr. Poonam V. Shivkumar (Medical Superintendent, Kasturba Hospital), Dr. Suchi Jain (Head, Department of Obstetrics & Gynecology, MGIMS), and Dr. Sumant Wagh (Civil Surgeon, Wardha).
Dr. A. K. Shukla delivered the welcome address, extending warm greetings to all speakers and delegates. Dr. B. S. Garg emphasized the critical role of midwives in maternal healthcare interventions. Reflecting on Mahatma Gandhi’s philosophy of serving the underprivileged, he highlighted that MGIMS and Kasturba Nursing School host the country’s first National Midwifery Training Institute (NMTI), where training for midwifery educators (NPMEs) is currently being conducted. He stressed the need for establishing a midwifery cadre to ensure a structured career progression for midwives and described midwifery as a game changer in maternal healthcare.
"Collaborative care is the key to strengthening maternal healthcare. Through holistic care, obstetricians can better address the mental health of pregnant women," said Dr. Poonam V. Shivkumar. She also firmly stated that "violence against women should not be tolerated," advocating for gender equity and a violence-free environment for women.
Chief Guest Dr. Pawan Kumar added, “With 2.9 million pregnancies annually and 1.5 crore deliveries taking place in government hospitals, strengthening maternal health services is the need of the hour.” He further elaborated on the future scope of midwifery in India, emphasizing that NMTIs and SMTIs across the country play a vital role in enhancing maternal healthcare. He also stressed the importance of early high-risk pregnancy identification and postnatal guidance.
The conference also featured distinguished speakers from Maharashtra, Madhya Pradesh, Tamil Nadu, Chhattisgarh, Uttar Pradesh, Bihar, and Assam. Senior obstetricians delivered insightful lectures on various aspects of maternal healthcare. Dr. V. B. Bangal (Professor & Head, Pravara Medical Institute) discussed the barriers and facilitators in the implementation of intrapartum care. Dr. Amita Pandey (Lucknow) elaborated on the role of birth companions in labor rooms. Dr. Charmila Aggavoo presented findings from the HAPPY study, which focuses on holistic healthcare for pregnant women, and also participated in a panel discussion. Dr. Shabana Sultan (Bhopal) highlighted the rights of pregnant women in the current healthcare landscape. Dr. Priyanka Singh (WHO) emphasized policy decisions and strategic planning for gender-sensitive, holistic, and collaborative maternal healthcare, free from intimate partner violence (IPV).
The conference concluded with a cultural evening and dinner. Technical support was provided by the Safe Motherhood Committee of FOGSI, led by Dr. Poonam Goyal from New Delhi. The event was held under the auspices of WHO and the Government of India.
